full_judgment:
4. On appeal the learned District Judge found that Sayera Khatun is wife of the pre-emptee, Shahajahan Ali Molla and, as such, she had knowledge about the pre-emption case but she did not come forward to exercise her right of pre-emption which right must be presumed to have been waived. The learned District Judge therefore held that the pre-emption case is not bad for non-joinder of Sayera Khatun. In that view the learned District Judge set aside the order passed by the learned Munsif and allowed pre-emption. The respondent thereafter moved the High Court Division in revision under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the learned Single Judge who heard the matter set aside the judgment and order of the learned District Judge and restored those of the learned Munsif following the decision of this Court reported in 33 DLR (A.D) 113, Abdus Samad and others Vs. Md. Sohrab Ali and others in which it has been held that omission of a necessary party is fatal to the pre-emption case. 

 8. It will thus appear that Sayera Khatun being found to be a co-sharer she was a necessary party in the pre-emption proceeding and the failure to make her party to the pre-emption proceeding has vitiated the pre-emption case. The mere fact that the respondent did not disclose her name does not absolve the appellant-pre-emptors from his mandatory duty to implead her by ascertaining necessary particulars. Because the pre-emptors could not be oblivious as to Ext. B(2) the kabala dated 2.6.73 by which Sayera Khatun purchased 1.40 acres of land out of the disputed tenancy and ought to have made her a party. The contention of Mr. Haldar is untenable because not only the objection was taken in the written statement about non-joinder of necessary party, Ext. B(2) would have clarified as to who has been left out. The pre-emptor did not take any step and failed to remove the defect.
